symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Common radius of the primitive \(C^{s}\) balls.

symbols.name: c_theta
symbols.def: Lower derivative bound on the dose-response curve.

symbols.name: C_theta
symbols.def: Upper derivative bound on the dose-response curve.

symbols.name: c_g
symbols.def: Strict-overlap lower bound for the conditional treatment density.

symbols.name: C_g
symbols.def: Upper bound for the conditional treatment density.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: Observed confounder vector, the first coordinate block of \(O\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Observed continuous dose, the second coordinate of \(O\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: Observed outcome, the third coordinate of \(O\).

symbols.name: Ypot
symbols.def: Potential-outcome coordinate process \(a\mapsto Y(a)\) taking values in \([-B,B]\).

symbols.name: Yspace
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Y_B\) is the space of Borel-measurable functions from \([0,1]\) to \([-B,B]\), equipped with the evaluation sigma-field.

symbols.name: Pfull
symbols.def: \(P^{\mathrm F}\) is a generic law of \((W,A,Y,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\})\) whose observed-coordinate marginal may equal \(P\).

symbols.name: muF
symbols.def: \(\mu^{\mathrm F}(a,w)\) denotes the jointly measurable conditional potential-outcome mean version specified by \(\texttt{ass:potential-mean-continuity}\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: A version of the marginal Radon--Nikodym derivative of \(W\) under the observed law \(P\).

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: A version of the conditional Radon--Nikodym derivative \(g(a\mid w)\) of \(A\) given \(W=w\) under \(P\).

symbols.name: f
symbols.def: \(f(a)=\int g(a\mid w)p(w)\,dw\), the marginal density of \(A\).

symbols.name: Rwit
symbols.def: \(R_0\) takes values \(-1\) and \(1\) with equal probability.

symbols.name: P0full
symbols.def: \(P_0^{\mathrm F}\) is the explicit full-data law constructed in \(\texttt{def:nonempty-witness}\).

symbols.name: Mpublished
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{WGC}}=\{P:\theta\text{ is nondecreasing and the marginal distribution of }A\text{ is continuous with positive density}\}\), the causal-isotonic model of Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020).

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: The fixed-radius causal-isotonic model defined in \(\texttt{def:model-class}\).

symbols.name: folds
symbols.def: \((\mathcal I_{1},\ldots,\mathcal I_{K})\) is a balanced partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

symbols.name: nuisance_hat
symbols.def: \((\widehat p_{k},\widehat g_{k},\widehat m_{k},\widehat r_{k})\) are boundary-corrected local-polynomial estimators of degree at least \(\lceil s\rceil\), trained outside \(\mathcal I_{k}\) with bandwidth \(h_{n}=n^{-1/(2s)}\); the two density estimators are normalized and stabilized on \([\varrho_n,\varrho_n^{-1}]\).

symbols.name: zi
symbols.def: For \(i\in\mathcal I_{k}\), \(Z_i=\{Y_i-\widehat m_k(A_i,W_i)\}\widehat f_k(A_i)/\widehat g_k(A_i\mid W_i)+|\mathcal I_k|^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal I_k}\widehat m_k(A_i,W_j)\), where \(\widehat f_k(a)=\int\widehat g_k(a\mid w)\widehat p_k(w)\,dw\).

symbols.name: Aorder
symbols.def: \(A_{(1)}<\cdots<A_{(n)}\) are the ordered doses, with \(Z_{(i)}\) carried along.

symbols.name: kappahat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\kappa(a)=\widehat f(a)\int\{\widehat r(a,w)-\widehat m(a,w)^2\}\widehat p(w)/\widehat g(a\mid w)\,dw\), averaged over training fits and stabilized on \([\varrho_n,\varrho_n^{-1}]\).

symbols.name: Wtwo
symbols.def: \(\mathbb W(0)=0\) with independent stationary Gaussian increments.

symbols.name: gcm_slope
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak g\) is the left slope of the greatest convex minorant of \(X\).

symbols.name: gcm0_slope
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak g_x^{0}\) is assembled from the left and right one-sided GCM slopes under the constraint that the slope at \(x\) equals \(2x\), capping the left slope above by \(2x\) and the right slope below by \(2x\).

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: Additive excess level and normalized cluster mark.

symbols.name: Rc
symbols.def: \(R_{\mathrm c}(x)=\inf\{R\ge0:\mathfrak g(t)=\mathfrak g_x^0(t)\text{ for every }t\notin[x-R,x+R]\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\).

symbols.name: Ru
symbols.def: \(R(u)=u^2\), the contact truncation radius and Brownian padding radius.

symbols.name: qrun
symbols.def: \(q(u)=\lceil\rho(u)/\Delta(u)\rceil\), the number of preceding mesh cells in one declustering run.

symbols.name: Au
symbols.def: \(A_u=\{D(0)>u,\ R_{\mathrm c}(0)\le R(u),\ D(-j\Delta(u))\le u\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,q(u)\}\), the Palm root event for a high cluster.

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: \(\lambda(u)=\Delta(u)^{-1}\Pr(A_u)\), the exact runs-declustered cluster intensity per unit canonical length.

symbols.name: Eclass
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak E=\{u\mapsto\beta u+\gamma\log u+c:\beta>0,\ \gamma,c\in\mathbb R\}\), the asserted centering-accuracy expansion class.

symbols.name: beta_star
symbols.def: \(\beta_{\star}\) is the linear coefficient derived by \(\texttt{thm:canonical-excursion}\).

symbols.name: gamma_star
symbols.def: \(\gamma_{\star}\) is the logarithmic coefficient derived by \(\texttt{thm:canonical-excursion}\).

symbols.name: c_star
symbols.def: \(c_{\star}\) is the constant coefficient derived by \(\texttt{thm:canonical-excursion}\).

symbols.name: Estar
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_{\star}(u)=\beta_{\star}u+\gamma_{\star}\log u+c_{\star}\in\mathfrak E\), with its coefficients derived by \(\texttt{thm:canonical-excursion}\).

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: \(\ell(u)\) is any deterministic selection satisfying \(\ell(u)\in\mathfrak L(u)\) for all sufficiently large \(u\).

symbols.name: decluster_handle
symbols.def: Contact-radius localization followed by Palm analysis of the exact root event \(A_u\), including the conditional GCM contact-set energy and translation mode.

symbols.name: T0
symbols.def: \(T_0=\max\{e,\exp[\mathcal E_{\star}(u_0)]\}\), so \(\log T\ge\mathcal E_{\star}(u_0)\) whenever \(T\ge T_0\).

symbols.name: bT
symbols.def: For \(T\ge T_0\), \(b(T)\) is the unique \(u\ge u_0\) satisfying \(\mathcal E_{\star}(u)=\log T\).

symbols.name: upilT
symbols.def: For \(T\ge T_0\), \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)=b(T)-a(T)h(T)\); the marked cluster process is used along the eventual subregime in which \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\ge u_0\).

symbols.name: NuT
symbols.def: For \(T\ge T_0\) with \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\ge u_0\), \(\mathcal N_T\) puts a point at \((j\Delta(u_{\mathrm p}(T))/T,\{D(j\Delta(u_{\mathrm p}(T)))-b(T)\}/a(T))\) whenever the level-\(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\) translate of the Palm root rule \(A_u\) holds at \(j\Delta(u_{\mathrm p}(T))\in[0,T]\).

symbols.name: DpadT
symbols.def: For \(T\ge T_0\), \(D_T^{\mathrm{pad}}\) is computed at the grid \(\Delta(b(T))\mathbb Z\cap[0,T]\) from the constrained and unconstrained GCMs of \(\mathbb W(t)+t^2\) restricted to \([-R(b(T)),T+R(b(T))]\), with the energy integral restricted to the same padded interval.

symbols.name: MsimT
symbols.def: For \(T\ge T_0\), \(M_T^{\mathrm{sim}}=\max\{D_T^{\mathrm{pad}}(j\Delta(b(T))):j\Delta(b(T))\in[0,T]\}\), the canonical finite simulation target.

symbols.name: Vhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n=\int_J\{\widehat f(a)\widehat\theta'(a)^2/[4\widehat\kappa(a)]\}^{1/3}\,da\), where \(\widehat\theta'(a)=\int\partial_a\widehat m(a,w)\widehat p(w)\,dw\) is stabilized on \([\varrho_n,\varrho_n^{-1}]\).

symbols.name: qhat
symbols.def: On \(\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\), \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}=b(\widehat T_n)+a(\widehat T_n)\{-\log[-\log(1-\alpha)]\}\); set \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}=+\infty\) on \(\{\widehat T_n<T_0\}\).

symbols.name: qsim
symbols.def: On \(\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\), \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\) is the empirical \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(n^2\) independent copies of \(M_{\widehat T_n}^{\mathrm{sim}}\), with mesh \(\Delta(b(\widehat T_n))\) and padding \(R(b(\widehat T_n))\); set it to \(+\infty\) on \(\{\widehat T_n<T_0\}\).

symbols.name: tauz
symbols.def: \(\tau_{\zeta}=\inf\{a\in J:\theta(a)\ge\zeta\}\), with explicit empty-set and left-endpoint conventions.

symbols.name: Hn
symbols.def: \(H_n=n^{-1/3}(\log n)^2\), the maximal dose width used in the quantitative local transfer condition.

symbols.name: Bprod
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak B_n=\max_{1\le k\le K}\|\widehat m_k-m\|_{\infty}\{\|\widehat g_k-g\|_{\infty}+\|\widehat p_k-p\|_{\infty}\}\), with each norm taken on the corresponding compact domain.

symbols.name: Rlocal
symbols.def: For each fold set \(G_{n,k}(a)=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_k}\mathbf 1\{A_i\le a\}[Z_i-\xi(O_i)]\). Then \(\mathfrak R_n=n^{2/3}\sup\{|\sum_{k=1}^K[G_{n,k}(v)-G_{n,k}(u)-\mathbb E_P\{G_{n,k}(v)-G_{n,k}(u)\mid O_j:j\notin\mathcal I_k\}]|:u,v\in J,\ 0\le v-u\le H_n\}\).

symbols.name: Gtransfer
symbols.def: \(\mathsf G_n\) is the four-part Gumbel-scale remainder condition defined in \(\texttt{def:gumbel-transfer-threshold}\).

symbols.name: Snoracle
symbols.def: \(S_n^{\circ}\) is obtained from \(S_n\) by replacing every cross-fitted pseudo-outcome \(Z_i\) by \(\xi(O_i)\) and replacing \(\widehat\kappa\) by \(\kappa\) in both optimized isotonic objectives.

novel.justification: This is an explicit bookkeeping convention for treating an observed law as the marginal of an admissible full-data extension. It is satisfied by structural potential-outcome data-generating processes after marginalizing the potential-outcome path, and it does not encode either identification or the excursion conclusion.
This is the necessary ordering of the fixed lower and upper slope bounds and is transparent in any strictly increasing dose-response model.
On the unit covariate cube, every normalized density with a fixed lower bound requires this inequality; the uniform covariate law attains it.
On the unit covariate cube, every normalized density with a fixed upper bound requires this inequality; the uniform covariate law attains it.
On the unit dose interval, every normalized conditional density with a fixed lower bound requires this inequality; randomized uniform dosing attains it.
On the unit dose interval, every normalized conditional density with a fixed upper bound requires this inequality; randomized uniform dosing attains it.
This is the necessary ordering of the fixed effective-variance bounds and permits constant conditional variance as in the explicit witness.
The inequality leaves room inside the observed outcome bound for a linear increasing mean and nondegenerate bounded noise, a directly interpretable regular submodel.
The fixed Hölder radius contains the explicit uniform-design linear-response law whenever it contains the displayed polynomial primitives.

This is a source-independent compatibility condition for the Lebesgue-density parameterization of the covariate law. It is satisfied by every normalized smooth density in the instrumental subclass, including the explicit uniform-design witness, and is not attributed to the broader causal-isotonic model of Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020).

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed from \(P\).
Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), \(Y(a)\perp A\mid W\) for every \(a\in[0,1]\).

Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), there exists a jointly measurable choice \(\mu^{\mathrm F}\) such that, for almost every \(w\) under the \(W\)-marginal of \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the map \(a\mapsto\mu^{\mathrm F}(a,w)\) is continuous on \([0,1]\) and, for every \(a\in[0,1]\), \(\mu^{\mathrm F}(a,W)\) is a version of \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)\mid W]\).

novel.justification: This jointly measurable continuous-version convention is maintained specifically to turn almost-every-dose regression equality into an exact-dose statement. It is credible when \(Y(a)=h(a,W,U)\) for a bounded jointly measurable structural response \(h\) that is continuous in \(a\), because dominated convergence gives a continuous conditional mean version; it is separate from consistency, exchangeability, and overlap.

assumptions.condition: \(p\) belongs to the radius-\(L\) Hölder ball \(C^{s}([0,1]^d)\).

novel.justification: This fixed-radius global \(C^s\) restriction is an instrumental strengthened regular subclass, not a condition attributed to Takatsu and Westling (2025). It is satisfied by covariate laws with smooth spline or smooth parametric densities whose coefficients range over a compact set inside the displayed Hölder ball.

assumptions.condition: \(g\) belongs to the radius-\(L\) Hölder ball \(C^{s}([0,1]^{d+1})\).

novel.justification: This fixed-radius global \(C^s\) restriction is an instrumental strengthened regular subclass, not a condition attributed to Takatsu and Westling (2025). It is satisfied by randomized or observational dose mechanisms with smoothly varying conditional densities, such as compact-parameter logistic tilts of the uniform dose law.

assumptions.condition: \(m\) belongs to the radius-\(L\) Hölder ball \(C^{s}([0,1]^{d+1})\).

novel.justification: This fixed-radius global \(C^s\) restriction is an instrumental strengthened regular subclass, not a condition attributed to Takatsu and Westling (2025). It is credible for bounded clinical response surfaces represented by fixed-knot tensor splines with coefficients in a compact set.

assumptions.condition: \(r\) belongs to the radius-\(L\) Hölder ball \(C^{s}([0,1]^{d+1})\).

novel.justification: This fixed-radius global \(C^s\) restriction is an instrumental strengthened regular subclass, not a condition attributed to Takatsu and Westling (2025). It is satisfied by bounded smooth location-scale outcome models whose conditional mean and variance are smooth on the compact dose-covariate domain.

The global two-sided covariate-density bound is an instrumental compact-design restriction used for uniform local-polynomial control. It is satisfied after a smooth probability-integral reparameterization in regular designs with a positive continuous density, including the explicit uniform-design witness.

The fixed global lower and upper bounds on the conditional dose density form an instrumental uniform-overlap strengthening of pointwise positivity. They hold under randomized uniform dosing and under compact-parameter smooth tilts of that design, and they are not attributed verbatim to Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020).

standard.name: Derivative bounded away from zero on an interior interval

definitions.name: Fixed-radius causal-isotonic model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M(d,s,L,B,\delta,c_{\theta},C_{\theta},c_p,C_p,c_g,C_g,v_{\kappa},V_{\kappa})=\{P:c_{\theta}\le C_{\theta},\ c_p\le1\le C_p,\ c_g\le1\le C_g,\ v_{\kappa}\le V_{\kappa},\ c_{\theta}/2+\sqrt{v_{\kappa}}\le B,\ L\ge L_0;\ \exists P^{\mathrm F}\text{ such that }\texttt{ass:observed-marginal},\texttt{ass:consistency},\texttt{ass:exchangeability},\texttt{ass:potential-mean-continuity}\text{ hold under }P^{\mathrm F},\text{ and }\texttt{ass:outcome-bound},\texttt{ass:p-smooth},\texttt{ass:g-smooth},\texttt{ass:m-smooth},\texttt{ass:r-smooth},\texttt{ass:p-bounds},\texttt{ass:p-normalization},\texttt{ass:overlap},\texttt{ass:g-normalization},\texttt{ass:monotone},\texttt{ass:strict-slope},\texttt{ass:variance}\text{ hold for the observed marginal }P\}\).

definitions.name: Uniform-design linear-response full-data witness
definitions.construction: Under \(P_0^{\mathrm F}\), let \(W\) be uniform on \([0,1]^d\), let \(A\) be uniform on \([0,1]\) and independent of \((W,R_0)\), and set \(Y(a)=c_{\theta}(a-1/2)+\sqrt{v_{\kappa}}R_0\) and \(Y=Y(A)\). Take \(\mu^{\mathrm F}(a,w)=m_0(a,w)\). Let \(P_0\) be its observed \((W,A,Y)\)-marginal; under \(P_0\), the primitive functions are \(p=1\), \(g=1\), \(m=m_0\), and \(r=r_0\).

definitions.name: Pooled cross-fitted AIPW Grenander primitive
definitions.construction: Estimate \((p,g,m,r)\) foldwise by the boundary-corrected local-polynomial construction \(\widehat\eta\), form \(Z_i\), and set \((\widehat\Gamma_n,F_n)\) to the two cumulative processes defined in the symbol table.

definitions.name: Continuum isotonic LR profile
definitions.construction: Compute the unrestricted projection \(\widehat u\) and each equality-constrained projection \(\widehat u^{a,t}\) on \(\mathcal C_n\), then form \(Q_n(a,t)\) and \(S_n(\theta)=\sup_{a\in J}Q_n(a,\theta(a))/\widehat\kappa(a)\).

definitions.name: Stationary Brownian--GCM LR field
definitions.construction: From \(X(t)=\mathbb W(t)+t^2\), take its unrestricted GCM slope \(\mathfrak g\), impose the split slope constraint \(2x\) to obtain \(\mathfrak g_x^0\), and set \(D(x)=\int_{\mathbb R}\{[\mathfrak g(t)-2x]^2-[\mathfrak g_x^0(t)-2x]^2\}\,dt\).

definitions.name: Contact radius and padded grid field
definitions.construction: Define \(R_{\mathrm c}(x)\) as the least symmetric radius containing the support of \(\mathfrak g-\mathfrak g_x^0\). At level \(u\), truncate contacts and pad simulations by \(R(u)=u^2\). At horizons \(T\ge T_0\), compute \(D_T^{\mathrm{pad}}\) from finite-window GCMs on \([-R(b(T)),T+R(b(T))]\) and evaluate it on the mesh \(\Delta(b(T))\mathbb Z\cap[0,T]\).

definitions.name: Palm intensity, expansion class, and uniform block regime
definitions.construction: For \(u\ge1\), set \(A_u=\{D(0)>u,R_{\mathrm c}(0)\le R(u),D(-j\Delta(u))\le u,\ j=1,\ldots,q(u)\}\), \(\lambda(u)=\Delta(u)^{-1}\Pr(A_u)\), \(\mathfrak E=\{u\mapsto\beta u+\gamma\log u+c:\beta>0,\gamma,c\in\mathbb R\}\), and \(\mathfrak L(u)=[u^3,\lambda(u)^{-1/2}]\). From the expansion coefficients set \(u_0=1+\max\{1,(-\gamma_{\star}/\beta_{\star})_+\}\) and \(T_0=\max\{e,\exp[\mathcal E_{\star}(u_0)]\}\). Only for \(T\ge T_0\), define \(b(T)\) as the unique solution in \([u_0,\infty)\) of \(\mathcal E_{\star}(b(T))=\log T\), define \(a(T)=1/\mathcal E_{\star}'(b(T))>0\), and then define \(h(T)\), \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\), and \(M_T^{\mathrm{sim}}\) from the padded grid field in \(\texttt{def:canonical-localization}\). The marked process applies the same Palm root rule in the eventual subregime \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\ge u_0\).

definitions.name: Exact contact-set Palm declustering rule and handle
definitions.construction: At level \(u\ge1\), use contact cutoff \(R(u)=u^2\), mesh \(\Delta(u)=u^{-4}\), run radius \(\rho(u)=4R(u)\), and run count \(q(u)=\lceil\rho(u)/\Delta(u)\rceil\). Declare a mesh exceedance to be a cluster root exactly when the translated event \(A_u\) occurs. The proof handle is Palm conditioning on \(A_u\) followed by small-noise analysis of the constrained and unconstrained GCM contact-set energy and translation mode.

definitions.name: Simultaneous LR profile band
definitions.construction: For the eventual-regime feasible critical value \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\), with its \(+\infty\) convention when \(\widehat T_n<T_0\), set \(\mathcal C_n(a)=\{t:Q_n(a,t)\le\widehat\kappa(a)\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}\) and extend data-cell endpoints monotonically over \(J\).

definitions.name: Threshold-crossing confidence set
definitions.construction: Map every monotone curve \(\vartheta\) satisfying \(\vartheta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\) for all \(a\in J\) to \(\inf\{a\in J:\vartheta(a)\ge\zeta\}\), retaining the empty-set and left-endpoint conventions.

definitions.name: Quantitative Gumbel-scale nuisance and primitive threshold
definitions.construction: The condition \(\mathsf G_n\) is \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=o_P(1)\), \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\), \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\), and \(|\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)-1|=o_P(1)\), each uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\). The first display is the product-bias threshold, the second is the centered local empirical perturbation threshold on intervals of width at most \(H_n\), the third controls variance normalization at an LR excursion of order \(\log n\), and the fourth controls Gumbel centering through the spatial clock.

statements.statement: For every observed law \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\) witnessing its membership, consistency, conditional exchangeability, strict overlap, continuity of the smooth observed regression version \(m\), and the maintained version convention \(\texttt{ass:potential-mean-continuity}\) imply \(\mu^{\mathrm F}(a,w)=m(a,w)\) for every \(a\in[0,1]\) and almost every \(w\) under the observed \(W\)-marginal. Consequently, for every \(a\in J\), \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)]=\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\), so every admissible full-data extension of the same observed \(P\) agrees on the exact-dose causal curve over \(J\).
statements.justification: This isolates the maintained continuous-version convention needed to identify a causal mean at every exact dose rather than only for almost every dose; the convention is not part of the excursion argument.
statements.gap: Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) develop the causal-isotonic estimand and identification framework; the exact jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version imposed here is an additional maintained convention rather than a condition attributed to that paper.
statements.consumer: It gives the AHA/CMS nurse-hours profile and its threshold doses a causal interpretation under the maintained conditions.

statements.statement: Under the fixed-constant compatibility conditions, the observed witness law satisfies \(P_0\in\mathcal M\); under \(P_0\), \(p=g=1\), \(\theta'(a)=c_{\theta}\), and \(\kappa(a)=v_{\kappa}\).
statements.justification: An explicit member prevents the fixed-radius and bounded-outcome restrictions from defining an empty statistical experiment.
statements.gap: The cited causal-isotonic framework supplies nonparametric examples but does not verify compatibility for this proposal's simultaneous collection of fixed constants.
statements.consumer: The witness gives a concrete oracle law for the prescribed PAVA excursion simulation and the homogeneous-reduction falsification check.

statements.statement: The observed-marginal fixed-radius model is a nonempty proper instrumental subclass of the published causal-isotonic observed-law model: \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M\subsetneq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{WGC}}\). Membership in \(\mathcal M\) means that the observed law admits at least one causal full-data extension satisfying the maintained continuous conditional-potential-mean version convention and also satisfies the global fixed-radius \(C^s\), interior strict-slope, bounded-density, and effective-variance restrictions.
statements.justification: The inclusion makes explicit that the excursion transfer theorem is asserted on an instrumental strengthened regular subclass, not on the full published causal-isotonic model.
statements.gap: Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) provide the broader monotone causal-isotonic framework; the global fixed-radius \(C^s\) restrictions used here are additional and are not attributed to that paper or to Takatsu and Westling (2025).
statements.consumer: Readers can distinguish which published causal-isotonic applications fall within the simultaneous calibration theorem and which require a separate extension.

statements.statement: Uniformly over the instrumental fixed-radius subclass \(P\in\mathcal M\), the construction in \(\texttt{def:cross-fitted-primitive}\) satisfies \(\max_k\|\widehat h_k-h\|_{\infty}=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n})\) for \(h\in\{p,g,m,r\}\), where \(\beta=1/2-(d+1)/(4s)>5/12\), and \(\|\widehat\theta'-\theta'\|_{\infty,J}=O_P(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n})\), where \(\beta_1=1/2-(d+3)/(4s)>0\). These are consequences to be proved from the strengthened fixed-radius conditions, not assumptions imported from a comparator.
statements.justification: This derives concrete nuisance rates on the explicitly instrumental smooth subclass before checking them against the separate Gumbel-scale remainder threshold.
statements.gap: Doss (2026) formulates pointwise product-remainder conditions and Takatsu and Westling (2025) analyze different local-linear uniform remainders; neither source assumes or supplies this proposal's common global fixed-radius \(C^s\) class.
statements.consumer: This gives practitioners a concrete learner regime under which the simultaneous LR calibration can be implemented.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), the explicit local-polynomial learners satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\). In particular, \(\mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n)\) and therefore \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=O_P\{n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\}=o_P(1)\) because \(\beta>5/12\); bounded foldwise empirical increments give \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\); and the smooth plug-in estimates give \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\) and \(|\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)-1|=o_P(1)\). More generally, whenever \(\mathsf G_n\) holds and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), optimized-value stability gives \(\{S_n-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))=o_P(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).
statements.justification: This separates the actual product, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds required at the moving Gumbel level from the stronger instrumental assumptions used to verify them.
statements.gap: Published pointwise causal-isotonic LR theory requires a nuisance product small relative to one cube-root neighborhood; the displayed conditions add the logarithmic accuracy needed after scanning order \(n^{1/3}\) dependent neighborhoods.
statements.consumer: The lemma lets later work replace the local-polynomial implementation by any learner collection that verifies the same four quantitative remainders.

statements.statement: Almost surely, the constrained and unconstrained GCM slopes differ only on a finite contact interval at every \(x\), the integral \(D(x)\) is finite and nonnegative, and \(D\) has a separable locally bounded stationary version. Moreover, the joint contact radius for all \(x\) in a bounded interval has a tail sufficient for independent truncation of well-separated Brownian blocks.
statements.justification: The continuum maximum and any declustering rule are meaningful only after the nonlocal GCM energy is localized and given a separable version.
statements.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) prove the one-point LR integral is well defined; the uniform contact-radius and local-boundedness statement for the translated field is not supplied there.
statements.consumer: It licenses finite-window simulation, block separation, and fine-grid approximation for the canonical calibration.

statements.statement: As \(u\to\infty\), \(\Pr\{D(0)>u,R_{\mathrm c}(0)>R(u)\}=o\{\Delta(u)\lambda(u)\}\), \(\lambda(u)>0\), and \(\mathfrak L(u)\ne\varnothing\) eventually. There are unique universal constants \(\beta_{\star}>0\), \(\gamma_{\star}\in\mathbb R\), and \(c_{\star}\in\mathbb R\) such that \(\mathcal E_{\star}(u)=\beta_{\star}u+\gamma_{\star}\log u+c_{\star}\in\mathfrak E\), \(-\log\lambda(u)=\mathcal E_{\star}(u)+o(1)\), and \(\lambda(u+x)/\lambda(u)\to e^{-\beta_{\star}x}\) uniformly for \(x\) in each compact subset of \(\mathbb R\). In the exact uniform regime \(\ell(u)\in\mathfrak L(u)=[u^3,\lambda(u)^{-1/2}]\), \(\sup_{\ell\in\mathfrak L(u)}|\Pr\{\sup_{0\le t\le\ell}D(t)>u\}/\{\ell\lambda(u)\}-1|\to0\). The expansion implies \(\mathcal E_{\star}'(u)>0\) for every \(u\ge u_0\), so the displayed definitions of \(b(T)\) and positive \(a(T)\) are valid only on \([T_0,\infty)\). As \(T\to\infty\) through this domain, and hence eventually with \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\ge u_0\), \(\mathcal N_T\) converges to a Poisson random measure with intensity \(dt\,e^{-x}dx\), and \(\Pr\{[M_T-b(T)]/a(T)\le x\}\to\exp\{-e^{-x}\}\). The padded grid target obeys \(\{M_T^{\mathrm{sim}}-M_T\}/a(T)\to0\) in probability on the same eventual domain. These growing-domain assertions strictly strengthen the one-location Brownian--GCM LR law of Banerjee and Wellner (2001), recovered at \(D(0)\).
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: simultaneous LR calibration requires the rare-event law of the LR energy field, not the fixed-point law.
statements.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) give \(D(0)\); Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) give extremes for argmax or slope error, not for \(D\).
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies reusable critical values for any regular monotone model whose local LR statistic reduces to the same Brownian--GCM energy field.

statements.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), uniformly over the instrumental strengthened subclass \(P\in\mathcal M\), the quantitative condition \(\mathsf G_n\) yields \(\{S_n(\theta)-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))\to0\) in probability. The oracle statistic admits a coupling with \(\{S_n^{\circ}-M_{T_n(P)}\}/a(T_n(P))\to0\), with common constrained and unconstrained contact localization, locally frozen coefficients glued by \(T_n(P)\), and an asymptotically equivalent maximum over the two one-sided limits in each empirical dose cell. Consequently, uniformly for \(x\) in compact sets, \(\Pr_P\{[S_n(\theta)-b(T_n(P))]/a(T_n(P))\le x\}\to\exp\{-e^{-x}\}\). At one fixed dose the construction recovers Doss's (2026) pointwise LR limit, while the continuum coupling and eventual-regime Gumbel law strictly strengthen that fixed-dose result on \(\mathcal M\).
statements.justification: The canonical theorem becomes causal inference only after the displayed Gumbel-scale threshold is verified and the actual optimized cross-fitted statistic is transferred on the instrumental smooth subclass.
statements.gap: Doss (2026) proves a fixed-dose LR limit under pointwise remainder conditions, while Westling and Carone (2020) prove pointwise primitive transfer; neither controls a continuum maximum at its moving threshold or asserts the global fixed-radius subclass used here.
statements.consumer: This delivers joint profile calibration for the interior nurse-hours--readmission curve rather than a collection of pointwise LR intervals.

statements.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), uniformly over observed laws \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)\to1\) and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\Pr_P(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\). On \(\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\), \(b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))=o_P(a(T_n(P)))\) and \(a(\widehat T_n)/a(T_n(P))\to1\). Hence the eventual-regime analytic critical value \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\), built from the exact Palm-intensity expansion, and the canonical-simulation critical value \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\), built from \(n^2\) copies of the prescribed padded grid target, satisfy \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\) and \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\); both critical values equal \(+\infty\) on the vanishing complement \(\{\widehat T_n<T_0\}\).
statements.justification: Pointwise pivotality does not remove the population-dependent number of effective LR opportunities, so the spatial clock must be estimated at the centering scale.
statements.gap: Takatsu and Westling (2025) estimate ingredients for Gaussian uniform bands, and Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) study a pointwise isotonic scale; neither propagates a plug-in LR clock through Gumbel centering.
statements.consumer: It turns the canonical law into a usable critical value without estimating tiny single-location tail probabilities from the observational data.

statements.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), the sets \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) are intervals, and \(\Pr_P\{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for all }a\in J\}\to1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\). The image construction in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) is therefore an eventual-regime simultaneous \((1-\alpha)\)-level confidence set for \(\tau_{\zeta}\) for every fixed \(\zeta\), including the empty and all-domain conventions.
statements.justification: Joint LR calibration should report the scientifically interpretable crossing doses and the whole curve with one common coverage event.
statements.gap: Doss (2026) reports pointwise LR intervals in the nurse-staffing application; the proposition uses a genuinely simultaneous LR critical value and a coverage-preserving inverse map.
statements.consumer: AHA/CMS analysts can report the nurse-hours level at which the readmission profile crosses a policy-relevant threshold with simultaneous uncertainty.

statements.statement: If \(f\), \(\theta'\), and \(\kappa\) are constant on \(J\), then \(T_n(P)=n^{1/3}|J|\{f\theta'^2/(4\kappa)\}^{1/3}\); once this deterministic horizon lies in \([T_0,\infty)\), Theorems 1--3 reduce to a stationary canonical LR maximum on that interval. At one fixed dose, the marginal statistic reduces to the Banerjee--Wellner law \(D(0)\).
statements.justification: The reduction checks both the spatial factor and the fixed-point normalization against known theory.
statements.gap: The fixed-dose reduction is known from Banerjee and Wellner (2001); the growing deterministic interval is the new simultaneous component.
statements.consumer: It supplies an oracle simulation benchmark and a falsification check for implementations before applying heterogeneous clock estimation.

statements.statement: Can the contact-set Palm handle in \(\texttt{def:declustering-handle}\) be completed for the exact event \(A_u\) to derive its conditional shape, translation mode, multiplicity law, and finite positive intensity, with enough accuracy to identify \((\beta_{\star},\gamma_{\star},c_{\star})\), verify the block-tail ratio uniformly over \(\mathfrak L(u)\), and establish every assertion of Theorem 1?
statements.justification: The small-noise energy scaling alone does not determine the prefactor, additive ratio, or extremal index; these are the genuinely open parts of the project.
statements.gap: Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) compute an argmax upcrossing intensity from Markov transitions, but no analogous Palm law is available for LR contact-set energy.
statements.consumer: A solution yields constructive simultaneous critical values rather than a leading-log heuristic or a quantile defined circularly from the unknown maximum.

sampling_model.design: Observational independent sampling from an observed marginal law \(P\in\mathcal M\); causal interpretation is uniform over every full-data extension \(P^{\mathrm F}\) witnessing membership, including the continuous conditional potential-outcome mean version required for exact-dose identification.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A fixed number of folds and explicit boundary-corrected local-polynomial learners with bandwidth \(n^{-1/(2s)}\) are used for \(p,g,m,r\) on the instrumental fixed-radius subclass. Their product bias, local centered empirical perturbation, variance-normalization error, and clock error must satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\); the pooled validation-fold pseudo-outcomes then define one Grenander primitive.
sampling_model.overlap: The conditional density \(g(a\mid w)\) is bounded above and away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous dose \(A_i\in[0,1]\), with inference restricted to \(J=[\delta,1-\delta]\).
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(W_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with compact covariates and bounded outcomes.

target_estimand: \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)]=\theta(a)\), jointly for \(a\in J\) and every full-data witness \(P^{\mathrm F}\) of \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\texttt{ass:potential-mean-continuity}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The limiting distribution is the integral of the difference of the squared constrained and unconstrained slope processes.
We study the extremal behavior of the stationary argmax process on increasing intervals.
A suitably standardized supremum of the Grenander-type estimation error converges to a standard Gumbel random variable.
The confidence intervals concern the continuous treatment effect curve at a fixed point and invert a likelihood-ratio-type test.
The paper provides general conditions for consistency and pointwise convergence of generalized Grenander-type estimators.
Approximation results for the supremum of an empirical process yield asymptotically valid uniform confidence bands.
The paper develops a bootstrap procedure for constructing uniform confidence bands from weighted local-linear estimation.

tldr: Pointwise causal-isotonic likelihood-ratio inference is available, but scanning a whole dose-response profile changes calibration because approximately \(n^{1/3}\) strongly dependent Brownian--GCM LR opportunities are encountered. For observed laws admitting a causal full-data extension under an explicit maintained continuous-version convention, the project works on a nonempty instrumental fixed-radius \(C^s\) subclass, derives the sharp Palm-cluster excursion intensity, additive tail ratio, constructive centering, and Poisson law of the canonical LR field under a fully specified cutoff, mesh, runs rule, padding scheme, and block regime, and defines centering and scale only on \(T\ge T_0\). A separate quantitative theorem verifies the product-bias, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock errors needed at the moving Gumbel level before transferring the result to a pooled cross-fitted AIPW Grenander primitive and constructing simultaneous curve and threshold-crossing confidence sets for nurse-hours and readmission.

project_justification.gap: The literature contains the universal fixed-point LR law, extreme-value theory for the Brownian-parabolic argmax and Grenander slope error, pointwise causal LR intervals, and smoothing-based Gaussian bands. It does not contain the high-excursion and cluster law of the Brownian--GCM LR energy field or an extreme-scale transfer for a cross-fitted causal primitive.
project_justification.niche: This leaves exact joint calibration of the established unsmoothed causal-isotonic profile procedure without a theorem, even though the entire scientific profile rather than one prespecified dose is routinely inspected.
project_justification.fill: Exact-dose causal interpretation is obtained under an explicitly maintained jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version convention, separate from the excursion theory. The canonical theorem fixes the contact radius, truncation and padding radius, mesh, runs rule, Palm root event, exact cluster intensity, expansion class, block regime, and eventual thresholds \(u_0\) and \(T_0\). On the instrumental global fixed-radius \(C^s\) subclass, a separate quantitative result derives nuisance rates and verifies the exact product-bias, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds needed for Gumbel-scale transfer. The remaining statistical results establish the observed-law spatial time change, feasible eventual-regime calibration, joint profile coverage, and threshold-crossing inversion; an explicit full-data witness proves nonemptiness.

related_work: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) supply the fixed-point Brownian--GCM LR functional; Theorem 1 strictly tightens that one-location result to the explicitly defined Palm intensity and growing-domain excursions on \(T\ge T_0\). Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) inform the extreme-value architecture through the Brownian-parabolic argmax and Grenander slope error, but their statistics do not encode constrained-versus-unconstrained GCM projection energy. Hsing, Hüsler, and Leadbetter (1988) supplies the cluster point-process framework used with the fixed contact cutoff, mesh, runs rule, and Palm root event. Westling and Carone (2020) and Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) supply generalized Grenander and causal-isotonic primitives, consistency, and pointwise limits; the full-data marginal bookkeeping and exact-dose continuous conditional-potential-mean version convention are maintained in this core rather than attributed to those papers. Doss (2026) supplies the fixed-dose doubly robust LR construction and product-remainder motivation; Theorem 2 strictly tightens that fixed-dose result to a continuum maximum only on the explicitly strengthened subclass. Takatsu and Westling (2025) provide neighboring local-linear Gaussian bands and verify bounded-outcome and uniform empirical-process conditions, but they do not assume the common global fixed-radius \(C^s\) conditions on \(p,g,m,r\) used here. Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026) provide bootstrap smoothing bands and are a methodological alternative rather than a dominance target. A public Doss--VandenBerg 2026 abstract and slides advertise multiscale adaptive shape-constrained simultaneous bands and already analyze nurse staffing, but no public archival theorem text was available for audit; no claim of narrower width, tuning freedom, adaptation superiority, or dominance over that work is made.
technical_internal_limitation: The deterministic Cameron--Martin scaling and the plateau witness with LR energy one and action \(9/8\) are diagnostics only. They do not establish the probabilistic tail rate, the additive ratio, the cluster intensity, or the Poisson limit. The early kill test must reproduce this witness and stable localization on oracle PAVA grids before the causal proof is developed; a verified failure of localization or additive-ratio scaling calls for an analytic counterexample and termination of this spine.
honest_scope: The sharp canonical excursion theorem, including the Palm-root intensity expansion, constructive \(o(1)\) centering, and cluster law in the stated block regime, is open and load-bearing. Its expansion defines \(b(T)\), positive \(a(T)\), marked processes, simulations, and feasible critical values only on \(T\ge T_0\). Exact-dose causal identification additionally maintains a novel jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version convention over every full-data extension witnessing model membership; consistency, exchangeability, overlap, and the smooth observed regression version then identify that version with \(m\). The common global fixed-radius \(C^s\) conditions on \(p,g,m,r\), the two-sided covariate-density bound, and the explicit learner choice are instrumental strengthened restrictions, not assumptions attributed to Takatsu and Westling (2025). The separate threshold theorem must derive \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=o_P(1)\), \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\), \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\), and relative clock consistency before causal LR transfer is available. The explicit uniform-design linear-response witness establishes nonemptiness. The model excludes flat stretches, vanishing overlap, growing confounder dimension, shrinking interior buffers, and mixed-smoothness regimes. The proposal claims asymptotically exact joint calibration for this LR profile, not optimal width, global tuning freedom, or superiority to Gaussian multiscale bands. Under homogeneous \(f\), \(\theta'\), and \(\kappa\), it reduces to a deterministic-horizon canonical maximum and at one dose to the Banerjee--Wellner law.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Banerjee and Wellner's Introduction, Theorems 2.1--2.3, the Brownian--GCM construction in Section 2, and Discussion A--B were read; Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä's Introduction, Theorem 1.1, and its Albin-condition proof architecture were read.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing Brownian--GCM, isotonic likelihood ratio, supremum, Gumbel, excursion, and cluster found pointwise LR laws and argmax or slope-error extremes, but no LR-energy excursion theorem.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the sharp declustered high-excursion intensity of the stationary Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio energy field, its additive tail ratio, an explicit centering accurate to \(o(1)\), and a marked Poisson limit for growing-domain maxima.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The fixed-point LR statistic is an integral over a global contact-set rearrangement. The first donor step that changes is Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä's upcrossing-intensity calculation for the Markov argmax process; it must be replaced by a path-space contact-set and Palm-cluster calculation for LR energy.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is immediate from Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä because both fields are stationary Brownian-parabolic functionals. Rebuttal: their Airy/Markov calculation tracks one argmax crossing, whereas an LR exceedance is a nonlocal difference of two GCM projection energies with clustered contact-set rearrangements.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Doss's Introduction, constrained estimator construction, Theorems 3.3--3.5, cross-fitting section, and nurse-staffing application were read; Westling and Carone's primitive-to-Grenander theorem statement and setup were opened.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair cross-fitted causal isotonic LR plus simultaneous extreme-value calibration returned Doss's pointwise LR intervals, Gaussian smoothing bands, and a 2026 multiscale talk, but no published extreme-scale LR transfer.
seed_details.kernel: Prove an extreme-scale coupling from a pooled cross-fitted AIPW Grenander primitive to the inhomogeneously time-changed canonical LR maximum, uniformly over a fixed smooth causal model.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Doss localizes at one deterministic dose and Westling--Carone transfer pointwise primitive fluctuations. The first changed step is simultaneous localization of both optimized PAVA objectives over random windows visited by approximately \(n^{1/3}\) candidate locations.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is a routine uniformization of Doss's pointwise theorem. Rebuttal: a pointwise argmin mapping does not control optimized LR values at a growing threshold over a continuum, and the required common localization, dose-cell reduction, and spatial clock have no pointwise analogue.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Discussion B of Banerjee and Wellner was read together with their fixed-point theorem and proof localization; it gives an independent-sum LR limit only for a fixed number of separated points.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for dense-grid isotonic likelihood-ratio joint limits found fixed-point and fixed-multiple-point results, but no observed-primitive phase frontier linking independence to the stationary LR field.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize the separation frontier for a growing grid of LR tests: asymptotic independence above the cube-root correlation scale, a translated stationary LR field at the scale, and a cluster-corrected maximum below it.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The fixed-\(k\) proof separates disjoint \(n^{-1/3}\) neighborhoods. The first changed step is joint localization when the minimum spacing itself is of order \(n^{-1/3}\), where neighborhoods overlap and the independence argument fails.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is merely the usual distinction between fixed and local alternatives. Rebuttal: the focal object is a derived grid-spacing frontier with three different joint laws and an explicit connection to cluster-adjusted multiplicity, not a restatement of one local alternative.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Doss's nuisance assumptions, product-remainder argument, and Theorem 3.5 were read, including the distinction between entropy control and foldwise sample splitting.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper found states a sharp learner-rate frontier for an isotonic LR maximum; nearby uniform Gaussian bands impose their own empirical-process rates but concern a different statistic.
seed_details.kernel: Give an upper transfer theorem and a matching two-law obstruction for the weakest primitive remainder rate at which a cross-fitted causal LR maximum retains its oracle Gumbel law.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The pointwise nuisance product need only vanish locally. The first changed step is to compare the primitive remainder with the LR maximum's centering scale after maximizing over the effective \(n^{1/3}\) locations.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: the threshold is dictated mechanically by a union bound. Rebuttal: the optimized GCM projection can damp or amplify structured primitive drift, so necessity requires a least-favorable remainder embedded in an attainable nuisance class rather than a formal maximum inequality.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Westling, Gilbert, and Carone's scale estimators, joint pointwise theorem, and concluding discussion of the bias--variance tradeoff for \(\kappa\) were read.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing semiparametric efficiency with the isotonic spatial normalization or volume clock found local scale estimation and feasible Gaussian bands, not an influence-function characterization for this integrated clock.
seed_details.kernel: Determine whether the integrated LR spatial-volume clock is pathwise differentiable on the fixed smooth model, derive its efficiency bound when regular, and construct an attaining cross-fitted estimator or an irregularity certificate.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The local scale in Westling, Gilbert, and Carone is estimated pointwise. The first changed step is differentiation of a nonlinear integral containing \(\theta'\); integration by parts may regularize some paths but not the full nonparametric tangent closure.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: smooth plug-in consistency already settles feasibility. Rebuttal: centering-level substitution requires a quantified law, while the regularity or irregularity of the derivative-dependent integrated clock is not implied by consistency.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä's Introduction, assumptions, Theorem 2.2, confidence-band discussion, inverse-process proof outline, and boundary conjecture were read.
seed_details.destination_search: The located boundary corrections address slope consistency or smoothed bands; no whole-support Brownian--GCM LR maximum law was found.
seed_details.kernel: Construct a boundary-corrected isotonic LR process and derive a whole-support maximum law that combines interior stationary excursions with boundary contact geometry.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä trim the boundary because the ordinary Grenander estimator is inconsistent there. The first changed step is the inverse-process localization at distances below \(n^{-1/3}(\log n)^{-2/3}\), where one-sided contact behavior replaces the stationary field.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: boundary correction followed by the interior theorem is automatic. Rebuttal: the maximum may be dominated by a distinct one-sided LR field, so equality of the interior and boundary centering requires a separate excursion comparison.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Doss's general flatness-index limit field and adaptive pointwise LR construction in Theorems 3.3--3.5 were read.
seed_details.destination_search: The public 2026 multiscale abstract claims smoothness-adaptive simultaneous bands, so broad adaptation is occupied; no public theorem text found an LR-field mixture or an extremal contribution formula across flatness interfaces.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a simultaneous LR maximum law when the monotone causal curve contains finitely many strict-slope regions and flatness interfaces, identifying which local universality classes contribute to the global extremal clock.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Doss freezes one flatness order at one point. The first changed step is simultaneous rescaling across interfaces whose correlation lengths and drift exponents differ, followed by comparison of their extreme centering scales.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: the Doss--VandenBerg bands already adapt over smoothness. Rebuttal: this seed concerns a different theorem-level object, the mixture and dominance of non-Gaussian LR excursion fields, but it is withheld because the forthcoming manuscript is not fully auditable.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Doss's fixed-point LR inversion and nurse-hours application were read, including the scientific interpretation of the monotone profile.
seed_details.destination_search: Discrete minimum-effective-dose bands exist, but no confounding-adjusted continuous-dose isotonic LR inversion with a Brownian--GCM joint critical value was found.
seed_details.kernel: Invert one joint isotonic LR profile set into simultaneous confidence sets for every threshold-crossing dose and prove uniform set coverage including empty and all-domain cases.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Pointwise inversion controls one vertical section. The first changed step is a monotone set-mapping argument from a jointly covered curve to the continuum of inverse thresholds, with endpoint conventions and feasible LR calibration.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: crossing coverage is immediate once a simultaneous band exists. Rebuttal: that objection is correct for the set-mapping step, so this seed is retained only as a corollary-level consumer and not as the proposal kernel.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The causal estimand and monotonicity setup of Westling, Gilbert, and Carone were read before assessing a policy-learning variant.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for monotone continuous-dose policy regret revealed that the topic supplies neither a nontrivial policy class nor heterogeneity in the decision variable; adding these would change the scientific target.
seed_details.kernel: Choose a dose policy under a cost constraint and derive regret from a joint monotone band.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Under a strictly increasing mean response and a deterministic monotone cost, unconstrained welfare maximization collapses to a boundary or a one-dimensional crossing.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: the optimal policy is immediate from monotonicity and the budget. Rebuttal: the objection holds in the supplied model.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Doss's observational sampling model and cross-fitted pseudo-outcome construction were read before testing whether a symmetry-inversion lane was available.
seed_details.destination_search: No known randomization group is supplied by the observational design, and imposing one would replace the model with an experiment or a sharp-null problem.
seed_details.kernel: Use permutation or conformal inversion to obtain finite-sample simultaneous causal-isotonic LR bands.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The pseudo-outcomes are neither exchangeable under dose permutations nor observed counterfactual residuals under the causal null.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: the symmetry needed for exact conformal or permutation coverage is absent. Rebuttal: the objection holds in the supplied observational model.

literature_map.settled: Fixed-point LR universality, argmax-process extremes, generic cluster point-process limits, and Grenander slope-error Gumbel laws are settled.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The closest newer monotone-inference papers remain pointwise or use smoothed Gaussian statistics. None subsumes the LR-energy excursion kernel.
threads: BanerjeeWellner2001 fixes the canonical constrained-versus-unconstrained GCM energy and proves only its one-point law.
HooghiemstraLopuhaa1998 obtains a fixed-window tail and a growing-window extremal law for the Brownian-parabolic argmax process by verifying Albin conditions.
DurotKulikovLopuhaa2012 transfers that argmax extreme theory to a slope-error supremum with a nontrivial Gumbel centering.
HsingHuslerLeadbetter1988 supplies the abstract compound-Poisson cluster framework but does not verify its conditions for a continuous nonlocal GCM-energy field.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No located source derives a sharp block tail, additive tail ratio, cluster intensity, or Poisson maximum law for the Brownian--GCM LR energy field.

literature_map.settled: Causal identification, cross-fitted pointwise Grenander limits, fixed-dose LR inversion, and smoothing-based Gaussian uniform bands are settled.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The public Doss--VandenBerg 2026 abstract and slides occupy broad adaptive simultaneous shape bands but do not provide public theorem text for the Brownian--GCM LR excursion or transfer claimed here; no width or dominance comparison is made.
threads: WestlingCarone2020 gives consistency and pointwise limits for generalized Grenander estimators built from estimated primitives.
WestlingGilbertCarone2020 gives the causal AIPW primitive, pointwise and separated-point limits, and identifies uniform inference as difficult because the process is non-tight.
Doss2026PointwiseLR constructs the constrained cross-fitted causal LR statistic and proves its fixed-dose limit.
TakatsuWestling2025 proves feasible Gaussian whole-curve bands for a debiased local-linear estimator, not an isotonic LR profile.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: The uniform high-excursion-scale coupling of optimized causal LR objectives to a time-changed canonical LR field is not occupied.

literature_map.settled: Fixed separated points and continuum slope maxima are covered on opposite sides of the proposed spacing transition.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The result is not subsumed by local-alternative theory because spacing, rather than null displacement, drives the frontier.
threads: BanerjeeWellner2001 states an independent sum of canonical LR variables for fixed separated testing points.
WestlingGilbertCarone2020 proves asymptotic independence at two fixed causal doses.

novelty_justification: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) identify the one-location Brownian--GCM LR energy but do not study the stationary field's rare-event geometry. Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) prove a Gumbel law for Grenander slope error through the Brownian-parabolic argmax process, whose transition calculation does not determine the exact Palm-root intensity of constrained-versus-unconstrained GCM energy clusters. Doss (2026) supplies a fixed-dose cross-fitted causal LR statistic and a product-remainder architecture, but not a continuum maximum. The proposed kernel is the missing sharp excursion and Poisson theory for the precisely specified LR field, followed by an extreme-scale observed-law transfer on an explicitly instrumental global fixed-radius \(C^s\) subclass. A separate theorem states the exact logarithmic product, local empirical, variance, and clock thresholds rather than attributing that subclass to prior work. The public Doss--VandenBerg 2026 presentation is disclosed as a broad simultaneous-band collision; because no archival theorem text was available, this core claims neither optimal width, tuning freedom, adaptation dominance, nor superiority over their multiscale Gaussian bands.
